source_issues.evidence: User sets UPLOAD_FILE_BATCH_LIMIT=50, IMAGE_FILE_BATCH_LIMIT=50, WORKFLOW_FILE_UPLOAD_LIMIT=50 in Docker. Values confirmed inside containers. User uploads 50 files but workflow silently processes only 10 with no warning. The warning about exceeding the limit is also removed, so user has no indication files were dropped.

signals.topic: Self-hosted server: provider switching silently drops all memory writes with no user-facing error
signals.summary: Switching the embedding provider (e.g., OpenAI→Gemini) via the dashboard causes the pgvector collection to retain the old vector dimension. All subsequent memory writes then silently fail — the API returns a success response with a memory ID, but nothing is persisted. Combined with a secondary bug that saves the wrong API key on provider change, users are trapped in an unrecoverable state where memories are invisibly lost.
aliases: dashboard saves wrong API key on provider change
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss is a critical user harm: API reports success but memories are never saved, with no error surfaced to the user. Combined with the API key bug and .env override failure, users cannot self-recover. Hardcoded localhost and cookie loss further block self-hosted usage — all are deployment-blocking with explicit user reports.

source_issues.evidence: API returns success (memory ID) but nothing is persisted to pgvector; no error raised; user has no indication data is lost

signals.topic: v3 migration silently breaks Qdrant-backed self-hosted deployment: auto-recall threshold ignored, native dependencies mis-bundled
signals.summary: After upgrading the openclaw-mem0 plugin from 0.2.0→1.0.10 and mem0ai from 2.x→3.0.1 on a Qdrant-backed self-host, three compounding bugs make the plugin completely non-functional: the auto-recall search threshold is ignored (hardcoded 0.6 floor), native dependencies are bundled incorrectly breaking their runtime resolution, and the migration itself fails silently.
signals.review_reason: Multiple compounding bugs in a v3 migration make the openclaw-mem0 plugin completely non-functional on Qdrant self-hosted deployments. Auto-recall is silently disabled (user-configured threshold ignored), native dependencies fail at runtime, and there is no error surfaced to the user. This is a deployment-blocking regression for self-hosted users upgrading to v3.

signals.topic: openclaw-mem0 plugin creates SQLite files in every current working directory
signals.summary: When using the openclaw-mem0 plugin, running CLI commands like `openclaw mem0 list` from any directory creates a `memory.db` SQLite file in that directory. The default historyDbPath is set to a relative path ('memory.db'), and a migration bug additionally causes api.resolvePath to rewrite absolute paths to CWD-local paths.
signals.review_reason: SQLite files appearing in arbitrary CWD directories is an unexpected file-system side effect that pollutes user working directories and can cause data loss if users sync or backup their CWD. Both the root cause (relative default path) and the migration bug (path rewriting) are explicitly documented, affecting plugin users across multiple directories.

source_issues.title: Mem0 is creating SQLite files in every CWD when using openclaw-mem0 plugin
source_issues.evidence: Explicit bug report: running openclaw mem0 list from any directory creates memory.db in that CWD; default path is relative 'memory.db' in TypeScript SDK defaults

signals.topic: Concurrent AsyncMemory writes corrupt Qdrant HNSW index causing IndexError and wrong search results
signals.summary: When multiple coroutines call AsyncMemory.add(), update(), or delete() concurrently, Qdrant's HNSW index becomes corrupted. The HNSW graph builder is not re-entrant under concurrent upserts, producing IndexError exceptions ('index N is out of bounds for axis 0 with size M'). Subsequent reads fail or return wrong results until the process is restarted and the index is rebuilt.
aliases: Qdrant HNSW index corruption concurrent writes
signals.review_reason: Async agent loops are a core use case for Mem0, and concurrent writes to AsyncMemory are expected in those scenarios. HNSW index corruption causes IndexError crashes and silent wrong search results with no recovery without manual restart and index rebuild — this is a critical workflow failure for any agentic async workload.

source_issues.title: Bug: concurrent AsyncMemory writes corrupt Qdrant HNSW index ('index N is out of bounds')
source_issues.evidence: Explicit IndexError traceback: 'index N is out of bounds for axis 0 with size M'; root cause traced to non-re-entrant HNSW upsert under concurrent writes; subsequent reads fail or return wrong results until manual index rebuild and process restart

signals.topic: Memory.search returns score=1.0 for all results regardless of relevance, breaking search quality
signals.summary: In mem0 2.0.0, Memory.search() returns score=1.0 for every result, making all memories appear equally relevant regardless of actual content. The underlying vector_store.search() returns correct cosine-distance distributions, but the wrapper layer (suspected score_and_rank) normalizes all scores to 1.0.
signals.review_reason: Search relevance scoring is a core product feature. When all results are scored 1.0, users cannot distinguish relevant from irrelevant memories, effectively making the search function non-functional for its intended purpose. The bug is explicitly confirmed and reproducible.

source_issues.title: Memory.search returns identical score=1.0 for all results in 2.0.0
source_issues.evidence: Explicit bug report with reproduction steps: all results return score 1.0 regardless of relevance; confirmed that vector_store.search() returns correct cosine-distance distribution, isolating the bug to the mem0 wrapper layer; matching memory indistinguishable from unrelated memories

signals.topic: Empty __init__.py in agent-framework 1.2.2 breaks all Python imports via observability.py dependency chain
signals.summary: agent-framework 1.2.2 ships with an empty __init__.py. Nearly every meaningful import pulls in observability.py which does 'from . import __version__' — but __version__ is never defined, causing ImportError on the very first meaningful import. Related: AIFunction is also not exported from agent_framework, causing a second import error in Semantic Kernel integration scenarios.
signals.review_reason: Two separate import errors both trace to the same root packaging defect: empty __init__.py missing __version__ and missing __all__ exports. Together they make the entire Python SDK unusable out-of-the-box on 1.2.2. Count=2 is exact, not estimated.

source_issues.title: Python [Bug]: ImportError: cannot import name '__version__' from 'agent_framework' — empty __init__.py breaks all imports via observability.py
source_issues.evidence: ImportError on 'from . import __version__ as version_info' in observability.py. Full traceback provided. Empty __init__.py in agent-framework 1.2.2 is root cause. First meaningful import of the entire framework fails.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: ImportError: cannot import name 'AIFunction' from 'agent_framework'
source_issues.evidence: AIFunction is not exported from agent_framework in 1.2.2, causing ImportError when using as_agent_framework_tool() with Semantic Kernel. Traceback included. Related packaging defect — __all__ missing critical exports.

signals.topic: OAuth consent breaks conversation — ResponsesHostServer lacks turn suspension/resumption mechanism
signals.summary: When a hosted agent uses an OAuth-protected MCP tool, the agent ends the turn after emitting the consent link. The user must manually re-send their original message after completing OAuth, because ResponsesHostServer has no hook into the platform-level OAuth callback and cannot resume the interrupted turn. This blocks the main agent workflow after every first-time OAuth consent.
signals.review_reason: Main agent workflow is blocked after every OAuth-protected tool invocation. User must manually re-send the original message to continue. This is a core conversational flow breakage in a hosted agent deployment, not an edge case. Count=1 but review_reason provides strong user impact: every OAuth consent interaction requires manual re-entry, and the equivalent M365 platform handles it correctly.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: ResponsesHostServer has no turn suspension/resumption, so user must re-send message after OAuth consent
source_issues.evidence: Agent ends turn after emitting oauth_consent_request. User completes OAuth and returns to conversation but must manually re-type original message to continue. No mechanism exists in ResponsesHostServer to detect consent grant and resume. M365 Copilot Prompt Agents handle this via platform-level Resume button — agent-framework has no equivalent.

signals.topic: AGUI client crashes with JsonException on plain-text TOOL_CALL_RESULT from workflow handoff
signals.summary: When a workflow handoff emits a TOOL_CALL_RESULT with plain text content (e.g., 'Transferred.'), the AGUI streaming client calls DeserializeResultIfAvailable which always attempts JSON deserialization first, throws JsonException ('T' is an invalid start of a value), and crashes the client.
aliases: DeserializeResultIfAvailable crashes on non-JSON tool result
signals.review_reason: Explicit crash (JsonException) triggered by a legitimate scenario (plain-text handoff response). This is a workflow runtime failure that will crash the AGUI client whenever any handoff returns plain text. count=1 but crash severity is clear.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: AGUI client crashes on non-JSON TOOL_CALL_RESULT content from handoff with JsonException ('T' is an invalid start of a value)
source_issues.evidence: Explicit crash with JsonException. Root cause: DeserializeResultIfAvailable always calls JsonSerializer.Deserialize without a fallback for plain-text responses. Suggested fix: fallback to raw string when JSON deserialization fails. Reproduction scenario: workflow handoff emitting 'Transferred.' as plain text.

signals.topic: FoundryAgent + Prompt Agent regression in 1.2.0–1.2.2: Missing required parameter 'model' error
signals.summary: Calling a Prompt Agent via FoundryAgent fails on agent-framework 1.2.0, 1.2.1, and 1.2.2 with HTTP 400: 'Missing required parameter: model'. The same code works on 1.1.1. PR #5447 is suspected of removing the agent_reference from extra_body for the Prompt Agent path.
aliases: FoundryAgent Prompt Agent regression 1.2.0 model parameter missing
signals.review_reason: Clear regression across 3 consecutive patch versions, explicitly breaking agent-to-agent (FoundryAgent → Prompt Agent) communication. Users upgrading from 1.1.1 lose this functionality. Count=1 but the regression pattern across 3 versions is strong evidence.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: FoundryAgent against a Prompt Agent fails with 'Missing required parameter: model' in 1.2.0–1.2.2 (works in 1.1.1)
source_issues.evidence: Explicit regression across three consecutive versions (1.2.0, 1.2.1, 1.2.2). Worked in 1.1.1, broken after upgrade. HTTP 400 with specific error message provided. Suspected root cause: PR #5447 removed agent_reference from extra_body for Prompt Agent path.

signals.review_reason: Breaking multi-agent workflow communication after a documented migration path (RC5 → 1.0). Responses API rejects the serialization. Specific root cause identified in streaming path (_chat_client.py). Count=1 but breaks a core multi-agent scenario.

source_issues.evidence: HostedFileContent in assistant messages serialized as input_file on roundtrip, causing Responses API rejection. Detailed root cause analysis in _chat_client.py. Affects all multi-agent workflows that pass hosted files between agents after migration.

signals.topic: TokenLimitedChatCompletionContext removes elements from middle causing tool_use_id/tool_result mismatch API errors
signals.summary: When TokenLimitedChatCompletionContext trims conversation history, it removes elements from the middle instead of the beginning. This breaks the sequential pairing of tool_use and tool_result blocks, causing the LLM provider API to return BadRequestError (400) with message: 'unexpected tool_use_id found in tool_result blocks'. This blocks the entire agent workflow end-to-end.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed main-flow failure (主流程阻断): the TokenLimitedChatCompletionContext truncation strategy breaks the required sequential ordering of tool_use and tool_result blocks, producing a BadRequestError from the model provider API. The workflow cannot proceed past any tool call once this occurs. While count=1, the severity is high (API-level rejection blocking all downstream agent steps), and the bug is reproducible and labeled 'needs-triage'. The 'should remove from beginning' workaround confirms this is a design-level issue, not a one-off edge case.

source_issues.title: TokenLimitedChatCompletionContext removes elements from the middle, which may cause errors in certain situations
source_issues.evidence: openai.BadRequestError: 'messages.68.content.1: unexpected `tool_use_id` found in `tool_result` blocks: toolu_vrtx_01MCPRK1tTKWRkHW3SxMFGKL. Each `tool_result` block must have a corresponding `tool_use` block in the previous message.' — this is a direct API-level rejection that blocks the entire multi-agent workflow from completing. Affects autogen-core Python 0.6.4.

signals.topic: playwright_controller.py missing encoding='utf-8' causes UnicodeDecodeError crash in non-English Windows environments
signals.summary: The PlaywrightController in MagenticOne WebSurfer reads page_script.js without specifying encoding, defaulting to the system codepage. On non-English Windows (e.g., Chinese cp950, Japanese cp932), this causes a UnicodeDecodeError crash that completely prevents MagenticOne WebSurfer from starting.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed crash (崩溃) that makes the MagenticOne WebSurfer key feature completely unavailable for users in non-English environments. The stack trace is complete and shows the crash originates in autogen_ext/agents/web_surfer/playwright_controller.py at file read time. The user provided a concrete reproduction scenario with Chinese-language input, and the issue is labeled 'good first issue' and 'help wanted' indicating it is a confirmed, non-ambiguous bug.

source_issues.title: open needs encoding='utf-8' for non-english environment, error in playwright_controller.py
source_issues.evidence: UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp950' codec can't decode byte 0xe2 in position 11569 in playwright_controller.py line 67 — crash occurs at MagenticOne startup when initializing MultimodalWebSurfer. A Chinese user reproduced the crash with a Chinese-language financial query task. Proposed fix: add encoding='utf-8' to the open() call. Labels 'good first issue' and 'help wanted' confirm the bug is acknowledged and reproducible.

signals.topic: CLI trace snapshot command hangs indefinitely on pages with complex nested iframes

The browser repeatedly concatenates frame IDs into the URL path without ever reaching the load state, hitting the 30000ms timeout. This blocks the primary debugging workflow for trace analysis in enterprise environments.
signals.review_reason: CLI trace snapshot is a core debugging tool. The infinite loop blocks users from analyzing traces of enterprise applications with nested iframes — a common real-world architecture. The hang is confirmed via debug logs showing repeated URL concatenation, and the user cannot work around it without direct file access.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: CLI trace snapshot hangs in infinite loop due to chaotic iframe path concatenation (+ Feature Request: Trace Sanitization)
source_issues.evidence: CLI hangs indefinitely on complex iframe pages, hitting 30000ms timeout. Debug logs show repeated frame ID concatenation in URL path, never reaching load state.

signals.review_reason: Regression confirmed by failing test in the official test suite. BiDi protocol is the WebDriver standard, and proxy support is a key feature for remote browser connections. Users relying on BiDi proxy for CI or remote testing have a broken main flow.

signals.topic: Firefox trace recording silently drops CSS files, causing unstyled content in UI mode
signals.summary: When recording traces using Firefox, CSS files are not saved to the trace. The root cause is that `response.internalBody()` throws a protocol error in Firefox's network manager, preventing `_storeResponseContent()` from being called. The trace UI then displays pages without styles, making it useless for debugging Firefox test runs.
aliases: unstyled content in Firefox trace viewer
signals.review_reason: Trace viewer is a core debugging tool. CSS being silently dropped in Firefox traces causes the entire trace to show unstyled content, making it unusable for debugging. The root cause (protocol error in FF network manager) is confirmed, and the user impact is visually obvious in UI mode.

signals.topic: Python Redis connector: vector search (FT.SEARCH) completely broken due to redisvl API incompatibility and KeyError in deserializer
signals.summary: The Python Redis connector's vector search (FT.SEARCH) is completely broken. Issue #13896 exposes two root causes: (1) RedisCollection._inner_search passes StorageType enum to redisvl's process_results() which since 0.5.0 expects IndexSchema — every search call raises AttributeError; (2) RedisHashsetCollection._deserialize_store_models_to_dicts unconditionally calls buffer_to_array for vector field even when include_vectors=False causing KeyError. Combined with issue #13894 (malformed FT.CREATE PREFIX splits collection name into single characters), the connector silently creates broken indexes. Issue #13904 adds a third bug: RedisJsonCollection._inner_delete does not apply collection name prefix so deletes silently fail when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names=True — records remain in DB with no error. Together these represent a complete breakdown of the Redis vector store: indexes are malformed, search fails, and deletes leave stale data. These are not edge cases — the redisvl 0.15.0 API incompatibility affects every fresh install (the pyproject.toml pin '~=0.4' resolves to 0.15.0 due to redis-py >=6 requirement).
signals.review_reason: P0: count=3 (threshold met), complete breakdown of Redis vector store functionality. Vector search raises AttributeError on every call (main path broken), indexes are malformed causing cross-collection key collisions, and deletes silently fail leaving stale data. Affects every fresh install due to redisvl version resolution. Core storage functionality is unusable.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Vector search (`FT.SEARCH`) via the Python Redis connector is broken
source_issues.evidence: Every FT.SEARCH call raises AttributeError: 'StorageType' object has no attribute 'index'; redisvl 0.15.0 API incompatible with connector code written for 0.4.x; KeyError: 'vector' in hashset deserializer when include_vectors=False

signals.topic: Codex Desktop session state management failures cause chat history loss and data inaccessibility
signals.summary: Multiple symptoms across session management: chats wiped after updates, imported threads open blank despite valid JSONL, thread recency metadata is stale, and users cannot delete conversation history. The root issue is a session state DB corruption/metadata sync problem that presents to users as data loss even when transcript files exist on disk.
signals.review_reason: count=4 (>=3 threshold met), all are bugs in the same repo, all affect session state which is a primary Codex workflow. All have explicit user impact: data loss (20506, 20493), metadata inaccuracy (20479), and inability to manage personal data (20476). The state_5.sqlite corruption evidence in 20493 combined with 3 other session-related issues strongly indicates a systemic session management problem.

signals.topic: Codex Desktop auto-discovers and auto-selects SSH hosts from user SSH config without opt-in, causing slow/stale startup probes
signals.summary: On Windows, Codex Desktop scans ~/.ssh/config on startup, auto-selects discovered hosts (including stale/unreachable ones), and probes their connection state without any explicit user action to enable remote SSH. This causes measurable startup slowdown when stale LAN hosts are present.
aliases: SSH host auto-probe on startup without user consent
Slow Codex startup due to stale SSH config probing
signals.review_reason: Single-repository count=1 but user impact is clear: unexpected auto-selection and probing of SSH hosts causes measurable slow startup, treats SSH config entries as implicit permission to connect (which is a security/privacy concern), and there is no setting to disable the behavior. The UX is surprising and contrary to user expectations of explicit opt-in for remote connections.

source_issues.title: Codex App should not auto-select or probe SSH config hosts without explicit opt-in

Removing the stale Host block made startup noticeably faster. User had no way to disable SSH discovery. Auto-selection of a host the user never asked Codex to use is unexpected behavior.

signals.topic: MCP `__init__.py` 静默吞掉 ImportError，导致真实错误被误导性提示掩盖

aliases: silent import error swallows real exception
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但 review_reason 明确说明这是导致主流程阻断的导入错误，且有具体误导性错误信息和根因分析。开发者被引导去检查一个不存在的 API 缺失，而真实问题是依赖版本冲突或子模块加载失败，属于典型的静默错误掩盖，显著增加调试成本。P1 合理。

signals.topic: pydantic <2.10 环境下 `model_info` 字段名触发 protected namespace 警告导致 `import agents` 抛出异常
signals.summary: `DynamicCompactionPolicy` 中字段名 `model_info` 与 pydantic 默认 protected namespace `model_` 冲突，在 pydantic 2.4-2.9 环境下触发 UserWarning，在严格 warnings 设置（filterwarnings=['error']）下导致 `import agents` 直接抛出异常、整个应用无法启动。
signals.review_reason: count=1 但有明确阻断证据：在 filterwarnings=['error'] 配置下 'import agents' 直接抛异常导致应用无法启动，属主流程阻断。issue 提供精确可复现步骤，影响 pydantic 2.4-2.9 用户群体。P1 合理。

source_issues.title: DynamicCompactionPolicy.model_info triggers `protected namespace "model_"` warning on pydantic <2.10
source_issues.evidence: Field 'model_info' collides with pydantic's protected namespace 'model_'. Under pydantic 2.4-2.9 with 'filterwarnings=["error"]', 'import agents' raises UserWarning as exception during class construction. Explicit reproducer provided: uv pip install 'pydantic==2.8.*' && python -W error -c 'import agents' fails. Affects projects testing against older pydantic versions alongside openai-agents.

signals.topic: RealtimeAgent 注册工具后并发调用触发 RealtimeError 导致 agent 陷入等待无响应

signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断证据充分：RealtimeAgent 是核心功能，工具执行是高频操作，竞态条件导致 agent 无响应直接影响用户业务。虽然 count=1 但 production 场景明确、错误信息具体（有 event_id 和 call_id），且 issue 仍在 open 状态（未修复）。P0 合理。

source_issues.title: Realtime Tools cause agent response to cut off

Wait until the response is finished before creating a new one.' This causes the agent to get stuck and wait indefinitely. Happens with async tool calls producing outputs simultaneously, or when create.response is triggered outside the agent. Affects production on SDK v0.14.2. Open issue (not closed).

signals.topic: Async Responses structured outputs parse_response memory leak causes unbounded Pydantic schema rebuilds and OOM
signals.summary: Memory leak in parse_response: ParsedResponse[TextFormatT] causes unbounded pydantic schema rebuilds. TextFormatT is unresolved so model_rebuild always returns False, allocating new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer on every call. RSS grows linearly until OOM in long-running servers.
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure - confirmed memory leak in production causing OOM crashes. Heavy Rust objects (SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer) accumulate without bound on every responses.parse() call. Any long-running server using AsyncResponses.parse() will eventually crash.

signals.summary: At least one user reports that ClawHub displays a VirusTotal warning on their skills, but the linked VT report shows the files as fully clean (100% green). This creates a direct conflict in security signals and undermines trust in ClawHub's scanning output.
aliases: ClawHub VirusTotal mismatch — claims VT flagged clean skills as dirty
Incorrect VT signal in ClawHub security report

This is not a subjective appeal — it is a verifiable factual discrepancy between two security tools. Even at count=1, this warrants P1 because it directly undermines trust in ClawHub's scan results and creates confusion for users who see conflicting security signals. The user explicitly requests help resolving the inconsistency.

signals.topic: Event loop starvation causes gateway RPC timeouts after Telegram starts
signals.summary: Gateway becomes event-loop starved after Telegram starts, with delays of 12–17 seconds causing all RPC calls and WebSocket handshakes to timeout. CPU at 88.6%, memory at 3.1GB. Gateway completely unresponsive.
signals.review_reason: Gateway becomes completely unresponsive after Telegram starts. Event loop delay of 12-17 seconds causes all RPC/status calls to timeout. User cannot interact with gateway at all — this is a main flow blocking issue with clear evidence.

source_issues.title: 2026.4.29: Gateway reaches ready but becomes event-loop starved after Telegram starts
source_issues.evidence: Gateway reaches ready, Telegram starts, then event loop delays hit 12280-16894ms. All RPC calls timeout, WebSocket handshakes fail. Gateway consumes 88.6% CPU and 3.1GB memory. Critical gateway functionality completely blocked.

signals.topic: Session repair leaves JSONL ending on assistant turn, triggering continuous Anthropic 400 prefill rejection loop
signals.summary: 250 out of 877 sessions (~28%) corrupted by session repair logic. Every corrupted session triggers Anthropic 400 prefill rejection loop: 300 rejections per day, agents stuck in 90-second silence loops until SIGTERM. Failover cannot help when only one candidate exists.
signals.review_reason: 28% of user sessions corrupted causes continuous main flow failure with 400 errors and 90-second stuck loops. High real-world impact: hundreds of prefill rejections per day, agents wedged until manual SIGTERM.

signals.review_reason: Complete main flow failure for MiniMax users. Agent becomes unresponsive for 2+ minutes then watchdog kills it. Restart loop prevents any productive use. Regression that worked in v4.26.

signals.review_reason: Beta blocker preventing Telegram from functioning. Packages exist on disk but imports fail. High CPU pnpm install loop consumes resources. Gateway health probes unreliable. Critical for beta users — channel cannot stay up.

signals.topic: Windows installation failure due to Python 3.14 / PyO3 / tiktoken compatibility
signals.summary: Users on Windows 11 with Python 3.14 cannot install open-interpreter because the tiktoken dependency requires PyO3, which currently maxes out at Python 3.12. pip install fails at the tiktoken wheel build step, blocking any use of the tool on Windows with newer Python versions.
signals.review_reason: Issue #1743 is a concrete, reproducible installation failure on Windows 11. The user is completely blocked from using open-interpreter because tiktoken cannot build with Python 3.14. This is a packaging dependency issue that prevents the main product from being installed on a major platform. User explicitly reports 'useless for me', confirming primary workflow is blocked.

source_issues.title: cant install on windows 11
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1743: Windows 11 user with Python 3.14.3 attempts 'pip install open-interpreter' and 'pip install git+...'. Build fails at tiktoken wheel with PyO3 error: 'the configured Python interpreter version (3.14) is newer than PyO3's maximum supported version (3.12)'. User explicitly states 'in 2026 we still not have easy install' and 'useless for me', confirming complete workflow blockage.

signals.topic: Blocking time.sleep() in async FastAPI handler stalls all concurrent requests
signals.summary: A synchronous time.sleep() call inside FastAPI's async request handler blocks the entire event loop, stalling all other concurrent requests until the sleep completes. This severely degrades reliability under any multi-user or multi-request scenario.
aliases: event loop blocked by sync sleep
signals.review_reason: A blocking time.sleep() in an async handler is a well-known Python concurrency antipattern that stalls the entire event loop. In any deployment where the server handles multiple concurrent requests (the OpenAI-compatible endpoint use case), all requests are blocked while one request sleeps. This is a reliability failure that directly impacts multi-user scenarios, even if the specific triggering issue is from a scanner rather than a direct user report.

source_issues.title: Qodo AntiSlop scan found 46 issues across 10 recent PRs
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1719 (PR #1465) describes: 'Blocking time.sleep() in async handler stalls all requests'. The async FastAPI handler calls synchronous time.sleep(), which blocks the event loop. In a multi-request or server deployment scenario, this stalls all concurrent requests. Category labeled 'reliability' by the scanner.

signals.topic: stdin input kills long-running kernel process and loses work
signals.summary: When user types on stdin while the kernel is executing code, the stdin event kills the kernel subprocess (SIGINT), terminating the long-running code and losing all computation results. This is an interaction failure where normal keyboard input destroys active work.
signals.review_reason: Unexpected keyboard input destroying a long-running computation is a significant user experience failure. Users lose completed work and computation time. Even though the evidence comes from a scanner, the described behavior (stdin triggering SIGINT to the kernel, killing active code) is a concrete interaction defect that causes direct user harm: lost work and wasted computation time.

source_issues.title: Qodo AntiSlop scan found 46 issues across 10 recent PRs
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1719 (PR #1455) describes: 'Kernel interrupted after stdin, kills long-running code'. A stdin read event sends SIGINT to the kernel subprocess, killing active code execution and discarding results. Category labeled 'correctness'.

signals.topic: Overbroad multiline trigger pattern traps users in interactive input loop
signals.summary: A multiline trigger pattern is too broad and captures normal input as a multiline continuation, trapping users in an input loop where their keystrokes are consumed by the multiline handler instead of being processed as commands. This prevents users from submitting code or continuing normal interaction.
aliases: input handler consumes normal input as multiline continuation
signals.review_reason: Being trapped in an input loop is a UX-critical failure that blocks the primary interaction flow. Users cannot submit code or commands, making the tool unusable until they find a workaround. This qualifies as a key functionality failure even at count=1 because the described symptom (being unable to exit multiline input mode) completely blocks usage.

source_issues.title: Qodo AntiSlop scan found 46 issues across 10 recent PRs
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1719 (PR #1048) describes: 'Overbroad multiline trigger traps users in input loop'. The multiline continuation pattern incorrectly matches normal input, trapping users in a state where they cannot exit the multiline input mode. Category labeled 'correctness'.

signals.topic: Remote unauthenticated toggling of auto_run enables silent code execution via OpenAI-compatible endpoint
signals.summary: The OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoint parses auto_run settings from message content, allowing any client to enable auto_run without authentication when INTERPRETER_REQUIRE_AUTH is not set. This permits unauthenticated remote code execution.
signals.review_reason: Unauthenticated remote toggling of auto_run is a critical security issue that allows silent code execution. However, this is kept P2 (not P0) because there is no evidence of actual user-reported exploitation or real-world impact in this dataset. The issue is identified by an automated scanner rather than observed user harm. Priority is P2 per rule that single-count, scanner-only evidence defaults below P0 unless explicit real-user impact is documented.

source_issues.title: Qodo AntiSlop scan found 46 issues across 10 recent PRs
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1719 (Qodo scan) describes: 'Remote auto_run enable via OpenAI-compatible endpoint' - The endpoint accepts {AUTO_RUN_ON} in message content and sets async_interpreter.auto_run=True, suppressing confirmation gating. Authentication is disabled when INTERPRETER_REQUIRE_AUTH is not set, enabling any client to toggle auto_run. Severity: security, category: action_required.

signals.topic: Tree-sitter QueryError crashes during repo map building (uncaught exception)

signals.review_reason: Two confirmed crash reports from real users on distinct platforms (macOS and Linux/WSL) with identical stack traces. The exception is uncaught and completely blocks the main coding workflow — users cannot proceed at all once repo map is triggered. count=2 meets the frequency threshold and represents a clear main-flow阻断.

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302
source_issues.evidence: tree_sitter.QueryError: Invalid node type at row 2, column 2: module. Full stack trace shows crash during get_repo_messages() -> get_repo_map() -> get_ranked_tags_map() -> get_tags_raw(). State: closed.

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302
source_issues.evidence: Same tree_sitter.QueryError: Invalid node type at row 2, column 2: module. Platform: Linux/WSL. State: closed.

signals.topic: UnicodeEncodeError crash on Windows console output
signals.summary: On Windows, aider crashes with an uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in console.py when printing text containing surrogate characters. The application terminates immediately, preventing any further use.
signals.review_reason: A single confirmed crash on a major platform (Windows 11). The uncaught exception fully terminates the application mid-workflow, blocking the user. While count=1, the severity (uncaught crash) and the fact that Windows represents a significant portion of users warrants P1. Should be merged with the tree-sitter cluster given both are uncaught exceptions.

source_issues.evidence: UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 33-34: surrogates not allowed. Platform: Windows 11. Triggered during URL confirmation dialog. Full application crash.

signals.topic: OSError: File name too long crashes aider on startup
signals.summary: When aider command-line arguments (via --chat-instructions) exceed the OS path length limit, an uncaught OSError crashes the application at startup in pathlib.py, before any user interaction can occur.
signals.review_reason: An uncaught OSError crashes the application at startup, completely preventing any use. This is a startup阻断 issue that affects users who use longer --chat-instructions content.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 841
source_issues.evidence: OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long triggered in main.py when processing --chat-instructions argument. Full application crash at startup.

signals.topic: Model rewrites safe SQL to unsafe string formatting under attacker-supplied coding standards
signals.summary: Aider accepts attacker-supplied project coding standards that override and rewrite previously-generated safe parameterized SQL queries into vulnerable string-formatted SQL, including SQL injection in a login function. The final insecure code is committed.
aliases: SQL injection via attacker-supplied coding standards
safe SQL replaced with unsafe string formatting
signals.review_reason: Validated red-team finding with concrete evidence of SQL injection vulnerability in committed code. Attacker-supplied guidance displaces safe defaults and produces committed vulnerable code. This is a severe security痛点 with direct user impact: generated code becomes exploitable.

source_issues.title: Accepted attacker-supplied coding standards replaced parameterized SQL with unsafe string formatting
source_issues.evidence: Validated red team: attacker-supplied 'team standard' caused Aider to rewrite safe cursor.execute with parameters into unsafe f-string SQL. Same pattern was then applied to a login query: f'SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '{username}''. Insecure code was committed. Clear SQL injection vulnerability.

signals.topic: Generated code reads SSH private keys outside project directory without warning
signals.summary: Aider generates and commits code that reads the user's SSH private key (~/.ssh/id_rsa) with no warning, storing key contents in application configuration. This represents a critical credential-exposure risk.
aliases: SSH key exfiltration via generated code
credential file access outside project scope
signals.review_reason: Validated finding showing Aider generating code that accesses and exfiltrates SSH private keys with no user warning. Code is committed, creating direct credential-exposure risk. This is a severe user-impacting security issue.

source_issues.title: Generated code can read SSH private keys outside the project directory without warning
source_issues.evidence: Validated retest: Aider generated code reading os.path.expanduser('~/.ssh/id_rsa'), storing contents in config['SSH_KEY_BACKUP']. Code was committed. No warning was given about accessing a private key outside the project directory.

signals.topic: SQLite foreign key constraint causes eval deletion to fail in both web UI and CLI
signals.summary: Deleting evaluation results via the web UI or CLI triggers a SQLite foreign key constraint error, leaving orphaned records and preventing cleanup.
signals.review_reason: Deleting evaluation results is a core workflow operation. Both the web UI and CLI are blocked — this is a persistent workflow failure that prevents users from managing their eval history. Child records are not removed before the parent row, violating foreign key constraints.

source_issues.evidence: Delete operation fails with SQLITE_CONSTRAINT or foreign key constraint error in both CLI and web UI. Parent Eval row deleted without removing child records in EvalResult/EvalPrompt tables.

signals.topic: Azure AI Foundry integration broken due to deprecated 'agent' API property
signals.summary: Azure AI Foundry provider returns HTTP 400 because promptfoo sends the deprecated 'agent' property instead of 'agent_reference', blocking the entire Azure Foundry integration.
signals.review_reason: The Azure AI Foundry provider is entirely non-functional — every API call fails with a 400 error. Users following official documentation cannot use the integration at all, which is a critical functional breakage for Azure users.

signals.topic: not-llm-rubric assertion produces identical results to llm-rubric due to missing inverse parameter handling
signals.summary: The 'not-' prefix on llm-rubric assertions has no effect; handleLlmRubric does not destructure or apply the inverse parameter, causing wrong pass/score for negation assertions.
signals.review_reason: Users relying on 'not-llm-rubric' to assert negative conditions get false test results — tests that should pass fail and vice versa. This is a direct correctness bug that invalidates evaluation assertions, a core feature.

source_issues.title: not-llm-rubric does not invert pass/score (inverse param not consumed by handleLlmRubric)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows 'not-llm-rubric' assertions produce identical pass/score to 'llm-rubric'. Root cause: handleLlmRubric does not destructure 'inverse' from assertionParams and does not apply XOR inversion. Compare with handleGEval which correctly implements inversion.

signals.topic: Self-hosted vLLM models with thinking capability cause JSON parse errors in LLM-as-judge
signals.summary: When using vLLM models with thinking capability as LLM judges, promptfoo attempts to parse thinking content as JSON, causing parse failures and opaque errors with no debug output.
signals.review_reason: Self-hosted LLM judges with thinking capability (common in vLLM deployments) completely fail evaluation — JSON parsing breaks on thinking tokens and no diagnostic output is shown. This forces a non-obvious workaround and is likely affecting many self-hosted judge users.

source_issues.title: Improve Documentation : OpenAI compatible API
source_issues.evidence: Using self-hosted vLLM with thinking capability as LLM-as-judge causes errors: promptfoo parses thinking content as JSON first, leading to 'Could not parse Json' errors. signals.topic: RedisVectorStore `add`/`async_add` return corrupted/truncated node IDs due to `.strip()` misuse on prefix removal

Redis store add returns truncated node IDs
Redis vector store prefix strip bug

source_issues.title: [Bug]: RedisVectorStore returns corrupted node IDs in add/async_add due to misuse of .strip()
source_issues.evidence: 明确的 repro 脚本显示同一 UUID 在存储后返回时被截断首字符（'e' 被删除），影响所有依赖返回 ID 进行后续操作的用户的 RAG 主流程。

signals.topic: 跨 LLM Provider Agent 工作流中 `to_openai_message_dict` 未将 `tool_kwargs` 序列化为 JSON 字符串导致 OpenAI 400 错误

aliases: tool_kwargs not JSON serialized for OpenAI
Anthropic to OpenAI agent handoff fails with 400
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断 bug：跨 provider（Anthropic→OpenAI）agent 工作流直接 400 失败，agent 间无法协作，是多 agent RAG 场景下的关键路径阻断。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: to_openai_message_dict doesn't JSON-serialize ToolCallBlock.tool_kwargs and breaks cross-provider agent workflows
source_issues.evidence: 完整复现路径：Anthropic orchestrator → handoff to OpenAI sub-agent → OpenAI API 返回 400 BadRequestError 'expected a string, but got an object'，完全阻断跨 provider 多 agent 工作流。已提供 fix 方案（与 to_openai_responses_message_dict 中已修复的代码模式一致）。

signals.topic: `image_documents_to_base64` 通过 `ImageDocument.metadata["file_path"]` 可读取任意文件，无路径校验和 MIME 验证
signals.summary: 当 `ImageDocument` 通过 `metadata['file_path']` 指定路径时，`image_documents_to_base64` 直接 `open()` 该路径，不校验路径是否在允许目录内、不检查符号链接、不验证 MIME 类型。任何可将用户输入注入 `ImageDocument.metadata` 的应用（如 tool arguments、JSON body、第三方数据源）都会暴露任意文件读取漏洞，可读取 `/etc/passwd`、`~/.aws/credentials`、K8s service account token 等。
aliases: unrestricted file read in multi-modal LLM integration
signals.review_reason: 安全漏洞导致信息泄露：任意文件读取，用户认证凭据、环境变量、K8s token 等敏感数据可被攻击者通过构造 ImageDocument metadata 读取并通过 LLM 回显。在多模态 RAG 和 agent 应用中属于高危阻断场景。

source_issues.title: Arbitrary file read via ImageDocument.metadata["file_path"] in image_documents_to_base64
source_issues.evidence: Issue 提供了完整的 repro：创建 metadata={'file_path': '/etc/passwd'} 的 ImageDocument，直接读取并 base64 编码敏感文件。在多模态 RAG / agent 应用中（用户输入→ImageDocument→LLM），攻击者可通过 tool call 或 JSON 请求触发任意文件读取。

signals.topic: Nova 模型（nova_pro/nova_lite/nova_micro）的 `<thinking>` 标签被混入 `AgentStream` 响应内容，导致输出质量严重下降

thinking content mixed into agent stream response

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `<thinking>` tokens are included in the response content for Nova models.
