signals.topic: CLI commands hang indefinitely instead of exiting cleanly (status, memory list, neural status)
signals.summary: Multiple CLI subcommands (`ruflo status`, `ruflo memory list`, `ruflo neural status`) print correct output but then hang forever, never reaching a clean exit. SIGTERM is required to recover. Canonical CLI bin handles this correctly but the ruflo wrapper does not, and a related HNSW/BM25 bug causes stored entries to become unsearchable.
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues converging on the same pattern: (1) three specific CLI commands hang indefinitely after producing output, requiring SIGTERM to recover; (2) memory search becomes completely broken after storing entries due to HNSW/BM25 bugs, making the memory retrieval feature fail silently; (3) ruflo wrapper hangs ~2 minutes on one-shot commands. All three are workflow blockages — users cannot use these commands cleanly and must resort to workarounds (timeout, SIGTERM). Confirmed root causes in closed bugs.

source_issues.title: CLI teardown hang: status / memory list / neural status print output but never exit
source_issues.evidence: Three commands print correct output then hang forever instead of exiting. SIGTERM required to recover. Root cause: long-lived backends (memory/neural) leave connection, handle, interval timer, or db client unclosed, keeping Node event loop alive. Other commands (doctor, agent list, swarm status, task list) exit cleanly.

source_issues.title: fix: HNSW index gap + RRF scoring crush in memory bridge (2 bugs)
source_issues.evidence: Two bugs cause stored memory entries to become unsearchable via memory_search: (1) bridgeStoreEntry() never adds to HNSW index AND storeEntry() skips HNSW on bridge success; (2) RRF scoring crushes BM25 when entry has no embedding (0.7*0 + 0.3*0.8 = 0.24 < 0.3 threshold). Both bugs make stored entries invisible to search.

source_issues.title: ruflo wrapper: one-shot commands hang ~2min + AgentDB Patch warnings leak
source_issues.evidence: ruflo status and ruflo --version hang ~2 minutes before exit because wrapper has .catch() on cli.run() but no explicit process.exit(0) on success. Also, '[AgentDB Patch] Controller index not found' warning leaks on every invocation because wrapper bypasses console.warn shim.

signals.topic: ruflo CLI plugin installation fails — marketplace JSON not found, plugin install rejected
signals.summary: Plugin marketplace commands (`/plugin marketplace add`, `/plugin install`) cannot locate the marketplace manifest JSON and fail to install plugins directly from GitHub repos. Users with local source can workaround via local directory import, but direct GitHub repo installation is broken.
signals.review_reason: Issue 1677: main CLI workflow (hive-mind spawn with Claude Code) is completely broken after update — tool prints '[OK] Claude Code launched' but no worker appears, which is a hard blocking failure of the primary use case. Issue 1676: plugin installation is a prerequisite capability that is broken for all GitHub-based installs. Both have clear user impact and reproducible symptoms.

source_issues.title: ruflo Cli not start after update
source_issues.evidence: After updating ruflo from 3.5.80 to 3.6.11, `npx ruflo@latest hive-mind spawn --claude --auto-spawn` prints success messages but never actually spawns a usable Claude Code worker. Output shows '[OK] Claude Code launched' but no interactive session appears.

source_issues.title: Ruflo plugin installation not working with claude code
source_issues.evidence: All three plugin install methods (`/plugin marketplace add ruvnet/ruflo`, `/plugin install ruflo-core@ruflo`, `/plugin install ruflo-aidefence@ruflo`) fail because Claude Code cannot find the marketplace JSON file. Local directory import is the only workaround.

signals.topic: daemon-state.json write-race: background daemon flush overwrites concurrent CLI worker trigger increments
signals.summary: When a background daemon process is running and an operator concurrently runs `ruflo daemon trigger --worker`, the periodic in-memory flush from the background process races on daemon-state.json and overwrites the CLI's atomic increment. runCount appears to not increment even when triggers executed, leading operators to conclude CLI triggers are failing when they actually worked.
signals.review_reason: Issue 1637: write-race on daemon-state.json causes silent data loss — CLI-triggered worker executions appear to have no effect due to overwriting. Issue 1636: MCP worker-dispatch returns fabricated 'completed' status without actually executing the daemon, making the entire worker dispatch API unreliable and misleading. Together these cause false confidence in worker execution state.

source_issues.title: daemon-state.json write-race: background daemon's periodic in-memory flush can overwrite atomic runCount increments from ruflo daemon trigger --worker
source_issues.evidence: Real-time probes show runCount=433 immediately after CLI trigger, but after background flush the persisted state shows runCount=432. The race causes CLI-triggered increments to be silently lost. Operators conclude CLI triggers aren't working when they actually did execute.

source_issues.title: MCP hooks_worker-dispatch returns fabricated completion independent of daemon; process workers --action list returns hardcoded demo IDs
source_issues.evidence: mcp__ruflo__hooks_worker-dispatch returns status:'completed' synchronously without routing to daemon — daemon runCount does NOT increment. The UI falsely reports worker completion. Only `ruflo daemon trigger --worker <name>` actually executes work and increments runCount. This is a fabricated/lying completion status.

signals.topic: Git commits silently injected with Co-Authored-By trailer without user consent
signals.summary: Every `git commit` created during a claude-flow session automatically includes `Co-Authored-By: claude-flow <ruv@ruv.net>` without asking permission or providing prior notice. This misrepresents contribution authorship, pollutes GitHub contributor graphs, and requires rewriting git history to undo.
signals.review_reason: User consent violation with concrete consequences: contributor graph pollution and requirement to rewrite git history. While count=1, the severity is high — this silently modifies user-committed authorship metadata and the fix requires destructive git history operations. Not P0 because it doesn't block the primary workflow.

source_issues.title: Co-Authored-By trailer added to commits without user consent
source_issues.evidence: Every git commit during a claude-flow session silently includes 'Co-Authored-By: claude-flow <ruv@ruv.net>'. No consent, no notification. Consequences: misrepresents contribution (commits are user's work with AI assistance), pollutes contributor graphs, requires full git history rewrite to undo. Expected behavior: tool should never add this by default; opt-in via explicit config flag.

signals.topic: guidance ab-test charges API costs for guaranteed zero-delta results due to executor design flaw
signals.summary: `ruflo guidance ab-test` with the default executor cannot swap CLAUDE.md between Config A and B because both configs read the same on-disk file. The benchmark always produces zero delta but charges ~$23 per run (20 tasks x 2 configs). The tool prints verdicts implying CLAUDE.md is ineffective when it cannot measure it at all.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed financial cost (~$23 per run wasted) with architectural root cause. The tool misleadingly reports effectiveness verdicts for a measurement it cannot perform. Clear cost loss from a design flaw, not an edge case.

source_issues.title: guidance ab-test: default executor cannot swap CLAUDE.md between Config A/B (zero-delta by design)
source_issues.evidence: DefaultHeadlessExecutor's isContentAwareExecutor returns false, so both setContext('') and setContext(claudeMdContent) are skipped. Both configs read identical on-disk CLAUDE.md — delta is architecturally guaranteed to be zero. Each run costs ~$23 (20 tasks x 2 configs) for a meaningless result. Tool misleadingly suggests CLAUDE.md is ineffective.

signals.topic: Browser startup hangs and crashes on Windows/macOS — daemon process termination, IPC failure, or Chrome relaunch on every CLI invocation
signals.summary: Browser process lifecycle failures on Windows and macOS cause startup hangs (16+ min pre-handshake, 0-byte stdout), Chrome process tree kill/relaunch on every CLI invocation (headed mode), and cumulative EOF failures after N commands with AgentCore. Users report complete workflow blockage, inability to complete first open, or forced migration to alternative tools like Playwright MCP.
signals.review_reason: count=5, multiple OS platforms (Windows 11, macOS 26), two distinct root causes (pre-handshake hang vs Chrome relaunch per CLI call) with different mechanisms. Issue #1308: 16+ min hang blocks first open entirely, 0-byte stdout with no error, user migrated off tool. Issue #1299: headed mode completely unusable on macOS 26, every command kills+relaunches Chrome, entire process tree replaced. Issue #1138: AgentCore open fails and spawns orphaned AWS sessions causing cost leakage. These represent primary workflow blockage across major OSes with clear user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: open hangs pre-handshake on Windows 11 (0-byte stdout, 16+ min) — distinct from #1138
source_issues.evidence: First open call hangs at IPC initialization for 16+ minutes with 0-byte stdout, no error emitted, daemon never produces a response. User migrated to Playwright MCP as workaround.

source_issues.title: `--headed` window dies and Chrome is killed+relaunched on every CLI invocation (macOS 26 / Darwin 25.x)
source_issues.evidence: Every CLI command sent to a headed daemon kills the entire Chrome process tree and relaunches Chrome in headless mode. Visible window disappears within ~1s. Reproducible on fresh ephemeral profile, affects both 0.25.3 and 0.26.0. Workaround (AGENT_BROWSER_HEADED env var) does not prevent kill+relaunch.

source_issues.title: AgentCore: open returns EOF / about:blank and leaves orphaned READY sessions
source_issues.evidence: Open fails with 'EOF while parsing a value' after daemon creation. Multiple orphaned READY AgentCore sessions accumulate in AWS per failing flow, requiring manual cleanup via `aws bedrock-agentcore stop-browser-session`. Confirmed by user with closed_at 2026-04-05.

signals.topic: wait --download command reports requested path but saves to default Downloads directory — breaks downstream automation trust
signals.summary: The `wait --download <path>` command reports success with JSON metadata pointing to the caller-requested path, but the file is actually written to ~/Downloads instead. This causes downstream wrappers to expose incorrect metadata and makes savedFilePath unreliable for automation.
signals.review_reason: Single issue but with direct automation impact: wait --download is a core command for automated workflows, and its metadata output is provably wrong (file saved elsewhere than reported). Downstream wrappers cannot rely on savedFilePath, requiring manual stat workaround. This is a data integrity issue that silently misleads automation.

source_issues.title: wait --download <path> reports requested path but saves to default Downloads directory
source_issues.evidence: wait --download reports savedFilePath === requested path in JSON output, but actual filesystem shows file in ~/Downloads with original filename, not the requested path. Downstream wrappers cannot trust savedFilePath metadata.

signals.topic: snapshot --json returns severely truncated accessibility tree over remote CDP WebSocket — regression from v0.19.0
signals.summary: Connecting via `--cdp wss://...` (remote browser) produces ~715-char snapshots vs ~4849+ chars locally. Interactive elements inside portals (Radix UI popovers, combobox, tabs) are missing. Automated steps that filter data.refs for interactive roles return 0 results, breaking remote CDP workflows.
signals.review_reason: Explicit regression from v0.19.0 (a known-good version). Remote CDP is a supported configuration. The truncation renders snapshot-based automation inoperable (interactive elements not in refs). Workaround of pinning to old version is suboptimal and blocks users from bugfixes in newer versions.

source_issues.title: snapshot --json returns truncated accessibility tree over remote CDP WebSocket
source_issues.evidence: v0.25.3 produces ~715-char snapshots over remote CDP vs ~4849+ chars locally. Portal-rendered content (Radix UI popovers) missing entirely. Filtering data.refs for role=='radio' returns 0 results. Regression from v0.19.0 where remote CDP worked correctly. Users must pin to v0.19.0 as workaround.

signals.topic: state field in config.json causes tab to close immediately after page load — works with --state flag
signals.summary: When 'state' is set in config.json (~/.agent-browser/config.json), the browser tab closes automatically immediately after the 'get text' command is issued, even though 'open' succeeds. The same state file works correctly when passed via --state flag on CLI, indicating a config parsing bug.
signals.review_reason: State persistence from config.json is a documented feature that silently fails in a destructive way (tab closes during automation). The same operation works with the CLI flag, indicating a code path divergence in config loading. P2 due to count=1 but clear user impact on authenticated workflow.

source_issues.title: state does not work in the way config.json
source_issues.evidence: Setting 'state' in config.json causes tab to auto-close after 'get text' command. Same state file works correctly when passed as --state flag. User confirmed: removing config.json restores expected behavior.

signals.topic: --user-data-dir with spaces fails on Windows — paths containing spaces not properly quoted in Chrome launch args
signals.summary: On Windows, passing --user-data-dir with a path containing spaces (e.g., 'User Data/Default') causes Chrome to receive malformed arguments and fail. The double-quote wrapping is missing, and agent-browser also auto-appends a second --user-data-dir, causing duplicate arguments. Users of browsers like Helium with spaces in profile paths cannot use the feature.
aliases: Windows path with spaces user-data-dir fails
signals.review_reason: Windows-specific path quoting bug in Chrome launch argument construction. Blocks use of browsers with spaces in profile directory names. Clear root cause (missing quotes + duplicate arg) with concrete reproduction. P2 due to count=1 and narrower impact (non-default browser + Windows).

source_issues.title: failed --user-data-dir on windows with Helium browser
source_issues.evidence: Browser with spaces in user-data-dir path fails to use profile correctly. Chrome receives unquoted path and a duplicate --user-data-dir argument (auto-appended + user-supplied), both with incorrect quoting. Only escaped double-quotes inside the value make it work.

signals.topic: Vertex Gemini thinking模式下tool-call事件的thoughtSignature元数据丢失，导致多轮对话阻断
signals.summary: 当使用@ai-sdk/google或@ai-sdk/gateway路由到Vertex Gemini 3 thinking模型并启用tools时，无参tool call的thoughtSignature被丢弃，下一轮agent步骤返回400错误，提示缺少thought_signature。
aliases: vertex thoughtSignature lost for no-args function calls
signals.review_reason: 同一根因（Vertex thoughtSignature在tool-call事件中丢失）出现在两个issue中，直接阻断多轮agent对话。用户提供明确错误信息和复现路径，影响使用Vertex thinking模式+tools的核心生产场景。

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/google streaming parser drops no-args function calls, losing thoughtSignature
source_issues.evidence: Bug reproduced on BOTH @ai-sdk/google parser (direct Vertex path) and AI Gateway server (gateway path). Multi-turn conversations break when first function call is no-args: response message ends up with zero signatures, next agent step 400s.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway: providerMetadata.vertex.thoughtSignature dropped on tool-call events when routing to Vertex Gemini
source_issues.evidence: thoughtSignature missing from tool-call events on response stream. callProviderMetadata never set on saved tool parts. Next agent step fails with: Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts. This is required for tools to work correctly.

signals.topic: Vertex priority service tier和labels无法通过SDK传递，企业用户无法使用优先调用配额
signals.summary: 拥有Vertex AI Generative AI Priority（按需付费优先层）访问权限的用户，无法通过@ai-sdk/google-vertex直接调用或通过@ai-sdk/gateway的BYOK路径使用priority tier，serviceTier和labels均被丢弃。
aliases: Vertex priority service tier not supported
signals.review_reason: 直接影响企业用户为Vertex priority tier支付的费用价值，两条路径均不通。虽有count=1，但review_reason明确指出用户已付费的配额服务完全不可用，属于关键功能不可用场景，P1合理。

source_issues.title: Vertex priority service tier + labels not propagated (direct provider rejects 'priority', Gateway BYOK drops both)
source_issues.evidence: 拥有Vertex AI Priority访问权限的企业用户，通过直接provider和Gateway两条路径均无法使用该功能。Bug1: 直接provider拒绝'priority'值。Bug2: Gateway BYOK同时丢弃serviceTier和labels。影响用户组织已付费的priority配额服务。

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock丢弃message content part上的cache point，导致prompt caching功能静默失效，产生额外成本
signals.summary: 用户为Claude消息content block附加cache point后，Bedrock请求中未包含缓存元数据，prompt caching不激活，使用报告cache_write=0和cache_read=0，用户承担全额输入token费用。
aliases: Bedrock prompt caching not working with content parts
cache points dropped on message content parts
signals.review_reason: prompt caching是Claude的成本优化核心功能，cache point静默失效导致用户明确配置后仍被收取全额费用，属于体验显著下降+明显成本损失的双重痛点。用户明确使用content block级别缓存配置但功能不生效。

source_issues.title: Bug: Bedrock drops cache points on message content parts
source_issues.evidence: 用户在content block级别附加cache point后，请求成功但缓存未激活：使用报告cache_write=0和cache_read=0。这导致用户期望的prompt caching节省成本完全失效，用户承担全额输入token费用。

signals.topic: Bedrock上claude-opus-4-7使用native structured output时请求被拒绝（Extra inputs not permitted），该模型的结构化输出生产路径完全阻断
signals.summary: 在Amazon Bedrock上使用claude-opus-4-7配合schema/Output.object时，SDK构造的请求携带bedrock不再支持的output_config.format字段，导致HTTP 400错误，完全无法在该模型上使用结构化输出。
aliases: output_config.format rejected by Bedrock for opus-4-7
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：该组合是生产上常用配置，Claude Opus 4.7是旗舰模型，structured output是生产必备功能，用户明确遇到HTTP 400请求失败。虽有count=1，但关键功能完全不可用，P1合理。

source_issues.title: Bedrock rejects output_config.format on claude-opus-4-7 when SDK uses native structured output
source_issues.evidence: 使用claude-opus-4-7配合schema/Output.object时，bedrock返回{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"output_config.format: Extra inputs are not permitted"}}。完全阻断该模型的结构化输出生产使用。

signals.topic: OpenAI兼容流式协议下function.name晚于function.arguments到达时，parser抛出TypeError导致tool call执行失败
signals.summary: 当provider/model在第一个tool_calls delta中发送id和function.arguments但不包含function.name，然后在后续delta中发送function.name时，过早验证name的parser在累积完整chunk前就抛出异常，导致tool call无法完成。
aliases: streaming tool call parser crashes on partial name chunk
function.name arrives in later delta causing TypeError
signals.review_reason: 直接导致tool call执行失败，对于使用OpenAI兼容流式协议的非OpenAI provider（如Fireworks等），tool调用在解析阶段即崩溃。这是核心agent工具调用功能的阻断性问题。

source_issues.title: OpenAI-compatible streaming tool calls fail when function.name arrives in a later chunk
source_issues.evidence: parser在第一个部分tool-call delta时就验证function.name，但name在后续delta才到达，导致parser抛出TypeError，tool call执行完全失败。类似#6687但涉及name字段而非空arguments。

signals.topic: Turbopack proxy.ts generates empty middleware-manifest on Windows, silently skipping all middleware/auth proxies
signals.summary: Turbopack does not register proxy.ts (Next.js 16 convention) into the middleware manifest on Windows builds. The build completes without errors but middleware never executes at runtime, breaking auth proxies, CORS handlers and request interceptors.
aliases: Turbopack Windows proxy.ts middleware manifest empty
proxy.ts not registered in middleware manifest Turbopack Windows
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: all middleware/auth-proxy functionality is completely non-functional with no error or warning. Users deploy expecting cookie-based auth redirects or request rewrites and find requests pass through unmodified. This is a production-blocking regression affecting the Windows + Turbopack combination.

source_issues.title: Turbopack: empty middleware-manifest for proxy.ts on Next 16.2.4 / 16.3.0-canary.3 (Windows; root and src/ placement)
source_issues.evidence: Middleware-manifest is empty when proxy.ts exists on Windows; auth redirects and request rewrites silently fail in production with no error or warning.

source_issues.title: Turbopack: empty middleware-manifest for proxy.ts on Next 16.2.4 (Windows; both root and src/ placement)
source_issues.evidence: proxy.ts middleware completely fails to register in middleware-manifest on Windows builds. Users have no indication of failure until auth/cors checks silently pass.

source_issues.title: Turbopack: empty middleware-manifest for proxy.ts on Next 16.2.4 (Windows; both root and src/ placement)
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as #93326/#93328: Turbopack treats proxy.ts differently from middleware.ts on Windows, producing empty manifest.

signals.topic: next/dynamic lazy chunks use stale module graph after source edits in Turbopack dev mode (HMR broken)
signals.summary: Turbopack does not invalidate lazy chunk hashes when dynamically-imported source files change. After any source edit, the chunk retains stale module references causing TypeError at runtime. Only a full next build resolves it.
aliases: Turbopack HMR broken dynamic imports stale chunks
next/dynamic stale chunk after source edit Turbopack
signals.review_reason: Dev experience is significantly degraded: HMR is completely broken for dynamic imports in Turbopack. After any source edit to a dynamically-imported module, the stale code continues running with TypeErrors. Forces rm -rf .next and full restart. This is a primary use case (SSR hydration control via dynamic imports) that is effectively broken in Turbopack dev mode.

source_issues.title: next/dynamic lazy chunk uses stale module graph after source edits (Turbopack)
source_issues.evidence: After editing a dynamically-imported module, the lazy chunk still references the old module graph. TypeErrors occur at runtime and the only workaround is rm -rf .next and full restart.

source_issues.title: Turbopack: next/dynamic lazy chunk uses stale module graph after source file changes
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as #93293: Turbopack persistent dev cache does not invalidate lazy chunks when their source modules change.

signals.topic: use-cache SWR (stale-while-revalidate) blocks indefinitely on Node runtime — always returns fresh data
signals.summary: In use-cache's SWR branch, await ignoredStream.cancel() synchronously waits for the source stream to close on Node runtime, making SWR behave identically to blocking-wait. Cached functions with revalidate config never serve stale data on Node.
aliases: use-cache SWR blocks on Node runtime
signals.review_reason: Core caching functionality is completely broken on Node runtime. SWR never serves stale data — every request blocks until the full regeneration completes. This defeats the entire purpose of stale-while-revalidate caching and makes any cached route handler on Node behave as if no caching exists at all.

source_issues.title: use-cache: `await ignoredStream.cancel()` blocks SWR on Node runtime (waits for source close)
source_issues.evidence: SWR stale-while-revalidate pattern is completely broken on Node runtime. The cancel() call waits synchronously for the full source stream to close, so the cached function always returns fresh data instead of serving stale. Any Node runtime route handler using use-cache with revalidate never achieves the performance benefit of stale responses.

signals.topic: experimental.swcEnvOptions polyfill injection not applied to server-side Node SWC compilation
signals.summary: When experimental.swcEnvOptions is configured, polyfills are injected into client bundles but not server bundles. Server-side code using TC39 Stage 4+ features crashes with TypeError in production despite swcEnvOptions being set.
aliases: polyfill injection missing for Node SWC compilation
signals.review_reason: Production blocking: server-side code fails with 500 errors when using modern JS features requiring polyfills, despite the framework configuration being set correctly. The isServer branch in SWC options does not apply swcEnvOptions unlike the client branch. This is a silent production failure with no compile-time warning.

source_issues.title: experimental.swcEnvOptions is not applied to server-side (Node) SWC compilation
source_issues.evidence: Server-side code using modern JS features crashes with TypeError in production even though swcEnvOptions is configured. The client bundle compiles correctly but the server bundle emits untranspiled code. Users are forced to manually inject polyfills for server code.

signals.topic: Turbopack production minifier breaks citeproc-js bibliography rendering (null reference error)
signals.summary: Production builds with Turbopack minifier cause citeproc-js to throw TypeError: Cannot read properties of null when formatting bibliographies with page fields. Dev mode works correctly.
signals.review_reason: Production blocking: citation and bibliography functionality completely fails in production with Turbopack minifier. Any academic publishing or documentation site using CSL styles is broken. Disabling turbopackMinify is not a viable production workaround.

source_issues.title: Turbopack prod minifier breaks citeproc with Chicago author-date bibliography
source_issues.evidence: Citation formatting completely fails in production with Turbopack minifier enabled. The citeproc-js page_mangler function for page range formatting produces null reference errors. Academic and publishing sites using CSL bibliography styles are broken in production.

signals.topic: npm 发布失败：最新 SDK 版本未同步到 npm 仓库
signals.summary: 最新发布的 SDK 版本 (1.19.41) 未成功推送到 npm，导致用户无法通过 npm install 获取最新版本，被迫降级使用旧版本或手动构建。
signals.review_reason: npm 发布环节失败导致主流程阻断：用户依赖管理被中断，无法通过标准包管理器获取最新 SDK，强制降级或手动构建。属于关键发布环节失败，有明确 CI 证据和用户报告（issue #282）。

source_issues.title: Latest npm sdk version not published
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 CI 构建成功后无法通过 npm 获取最新版本 1.19.41，npm 上缺失该版本，阻断用户正常依赖更新流程。

signals.topic: getProjects API 响应 Zod schema 校验失败
signals.summary: getProjects API 响应与 SDK 内置 Zod schema 不匹配，导致大量项目字段（alias、security 等）报 required 错误和 union 类型校验错误，直接阻断用户调用该接口获取项目列表的流程。
signals.review_reason: 核心 API 接口响应校验失败直接阻断主流程：getProjects 是获取项目列表的基础接口，schema 不匹配导致该接口完全不可用，用户无法查询项目信息。有详细 ZodError 堆栈和 6 条评论持续讨论，属于用户高频使用场景下的明确阻断问题。

source_issues.title: `getProjects` response validation error
source_issues.evidence: 升级 SDK 1.18.7 -> 1.18.9 后，getProjects 调用报 ZodError：alias 字段期望 array 收到 undefined；security 字段 union 校验失败；约 45 个项目全部触发此错误。6 条评论表明持续活跃的问题。

signals.topic: turbo prune overmatches .gitignore patterns, causing files to be excluded from prune output
signals.summary: turbo prune uses .gitignore rules too broadly (prefix matching without anchor awareness), so explicit paths like /apps/app-a/coverage incorrectly exclude nested paths like /apps/app-a/src/api/coverage/. This makes prune output incomplete and blocks monorepo artifact export workflows.
signals.review_reason: Real workflow blocking: turbo prune output is silently incomplete, meaning monorepo artifact export (e.g., Docker builds via prune) ships fewer files than expected. This is non-fatal but directly breaks a core use case of prune. One distinct issue confirmed.

source_issues.title: `turbo prune` is overmatching .gitignore entries
source_issues.evidence: Files under /apps/app-a/src/api/coverage/ are silently excluded from prune output because .gitignore contains /apps/app-a/coverage. Verified by repro: file missing from out/ when using --use-gitignore=true; present when --use-gitignore=false. Root cause traced to WalkBuilder in turborepo-fs with parents=false.

signals.topic: Turbo fails to parse pnpm 11 lockfiles with new flat-string patchedDependencies format
signals.summary: pnpm 11 changed the on-disk format of patchedDependencies from a struct {path, hash} to a flat hash string. Turbo's PatchFile struct is typed as a fixed struct, causing serde_yaml to fail. Every turbo run emits a noisy WARNING and falls back to degraded cache invalidation (file-content hashing instead of lockfile-aware). Affects all pnpm 11 monorepos that use pnpm patch.
signals.review_reason: Significant CI impact: every turbo run on pnpm 11 with patches emits a persistent WARNING and loses lockfile-aware cache invalidation. This is a recurring cost/happiness problem on every build run. One confirmed issue.

source_issues.title: Turbo cannot parse pnpm 11 lockfiles with new flat-string `patchedDependencies` format
source_issues.evidence: WARNING on every turbo run: 'An issue occurred while attempting to parse pnpm-lock.yaml. Could not resolve workspaces. Unable to convert to yaml: patchedDependencies...invalid type: string, expected struct PatchFile'. Cache invalidation degrades to file-content hashing. Root cause in PatchFile struct in turborepo-lockfiles/pnpm/data.rs.

signals.topic: Turbo fails to parse pnpm 11 lockfiles with multi-document YAML format (configDependencies)
signals.summary: pnpm 11 writes multi-document YAML lockfiles with a pnpmfileChecksum frontmatter section. Turbo's lockfile parser cannot handle multi-document YAML. When configDependencies are present, this causes task failures (not just warnings) because the pnpmfile hook cannot be resolved.
signals.review_reason: Task-level failure caused by turbo's inability to handle pnpm 11 multi-document YAML: tasks fail outright when configDependencies are used. This is a complete workflow block for affected users. One confirmed issue, since closed (fixed in PR).

source_issues.title: Turbo cannot parse pnpm 11 lockfiles with multi-document YAML (configDependencies)
source_issues.evidence: WARNING: 'Unable to convert to yaml: deserializing from YAML containing more than one document is not supported'. When configDependencies present, tasks fail with 'Error during pnpmfile execution: Cannot find module'. pnpm -r run (without turbo) works correctly, proving turbo is the culprit. Fixed in PR #12616.

signals.topic: Schema.json URL (v2-9-5.turborepo.dev) redirects to Okta authentication, blocking public schema access
signals.summary: The versioned schema.json URL (v2-9-5.turborepo.dev/schema.json) now requires Okta authentication instead of serving publicly. This breaks tooling that fetches the schema for validation or IDE integration (e.g., schema references in turbo.json are publicly documented as resolvable).
signals.review_reason: Blocks public schema fetching for validation tooling. Impact is real but scope is limited to users relying on the versioned public URL (count=1, single affected use case). Marked P2 rather than P1.

source_issues.title: https://v2-9-5.turborepo.dev/schema.json redirects to Okta
source_issues.evidence: User expects schema.json to be publicly accessible (as it was before); instead, navigating to the URL triggers an Okta redirect, preventing schema fetch for validation tooling.

signals.topic: Graceful shutdown does not work on Windows (PowerShell / CMD)
signals.summary: On Windows (PowerShell/CMD), turbo kills child tasks immediately on SIGINT instead of allowing them to shut down gracefully. This is in contrast to WSL/Linux behavior where turbo waits for tasks to complete graceful shutdown. Results in tasks being aborted mid-operation on Windows.
signals.review_reason: Platform-specific but significant: Windows users' long-running tasks are killed without graceful shutdown, risking data loss or incomplete state for services started via turbo. Clear user impact and explicit platform comparison confirms this is a real regression.

source_issues.title: Graceful shutdown does not work on Windows (PowerShell / CMD)
source_issues.evidence: On Windows PowerShell, turbo exits in 1.013s without waiting (process killed immediately). On WSL, same turbo version waits up to 5.95s and completes graceful shutdown. Reproducer repo available at ygrandgirard/turborepo-graceful-shutdown. Confirmed by comparison of WSL vs PowerShell output showing 'Graceful shutdown end' only in WSL.

signals.topic: vercel env add --sensitive combined with --value/--yes silently saves empty string instead of actual value
signals.summary: When `vercel env add` is invoked with `--sensitive --yes --value <V>`, the CLI reports success (exit 0) but stores an empty string. The var appears as "Encrypted" in `vercel env ls`, masking the corruption. Diagnosed only after hours of production failures and `vercel env pull` revealing length-0 values. Reproduced on CLI v50.42.0 and v51.6.1. No error or warning is emitted.
aliases: --sensitive flag silently corrupts env var value
vercel env add empty value when using sensitive flag
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption in a core CLI command (vercel env add) that is indistinguishable from success. Production-deploys break silently with no warning. This is a main-flow failure with clear user impact evidence (hours of debugging, production failures). Matches P0: main-flow blocking with explicit user impact.

source_issues.title: vercel env add --value V --sensitive --yes silently saves empty string
source_issues.evidence: CLI reports success (exit 0) but stores empty string. Reproduced on v50.42.0 and v51.6.1. Impact: silently breaks production deploys — hours of confusion before diagnosing via vercel env pull revealing length-0 values.

signals.topic: vercel env add preview fails with git_branch_required despite CLI hint claiming the same command shape succeeds
signals.summary: `vercel env add MY_VAR preview` (without git branch) fails with `git_branch_required` on both CLI v50.32.5 and v52.0.0. Critically, the error's own `hint.next[]` suggests the exact same command shape (`vercel env add MY_VAR preview --value <value> --yes`) will succeed — then the CLI rejects it with the same error code. The hint and behavior are in direct contradiction. The REST API works correctly (omitting gitBranch applies to all preview branches).
aliases: vercel env add preview regression git_branch_required
CLI hint contradicts actual behavior for preview env add
signals.review_reason: A regression in a core CLI workflow (adding preview env vars) where the error message's own hint is self-contradictory. This blocks the intended workflow and forces users to the REST API. Primary flow is clearly blocked. Matches P0 despite count=1 because review_reason provides strong user-impact evidence: complete workflow regression on both latest and prior major CLI versions.

source_issues.title: vercel env add NAME preview (without git branch) fails with git_branch_required despite CLI hint suggesting it works
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on v50.32.5 and v52.0.0. Error hint explicitly suggests the exact command that is then rejected. Teams must fall back to REST API for every preview env var addition. Regression from previously-working behavior.

signals.topic: vercel env add stdin pipe silently truncates multiline values (PEM keys, etc.) to first line only
signals.summary: When piping multiline values (e.g., PEM private keys) to `vercel env add` via stdin (pipe or file redirect), only the first line is captured. Everything after the first newline is silently dropped. The CLI reports success ("Added Environment Variable") with no warning. This destroys secrets — Firebase Admin SDK and any library expecting a full PEM key fails at runtime with cryptic "Cannot read properties of null" errors. Reproduced on CLI v41.6.2 and v50.14.0.
aliases: vercel env add drops content after first newline on stdin
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption of secrets (PEM keys) via stdin in a core CLI command. The CLI reports success while silently destroying secret values. Reproduced across two major CLI versions spanning ~9 months. Runtime failures in production from truncated keys. Matches P0: silent data loss with clear user impact evidence (cryptic runtime errors, ~1700+ chars reduced to 29-52 chars).

source_issues.title: vercel env add truncates multiline values when piped via stdin
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on v41.6.2 and v50.14.0. Truncation is invisible at set-time (CLI reports success). Full PEM keys (~1700+ chars) are reduced to ~29-52 chars. Firebase Admin SDK fails at runtime. Only workaround is the Dashboard web UI.

signals.topic: Next.js 16 post-build validation drops intermediate path segments from multi-segment Root Directory causing ENOENT
signals.summary: When a project has a multi-segment Root Directory (e.g., `clients/admin-ui`) with a custom Build Command, Next.js 16's post-build validation computes expected file paths using only the basename (`admin-ui`) instead of the full path (`clients/admin-ui`). This causes ENOENT errors on files that actually exist on disk at the correct location. The build itself completes successfully; only the post-build validation step fails, blocking the deploy.
aliases: Next.js 16 post-build validation wrong base path for multi-segment Root Directory
ENOENT in post-build validation with monorepo Root Directory
signals.review_reason: Deploy-blocking regression for monorepo users with multi-segment Root Directory on Next.js 16. Post-build validation fails and blocks the deploy despite the build itself succeeding. Impact is blocking but affects a specific configuration (multi-segment root + custom build command + Next.js 16). Count=1 so P1 is appropriate per priority rules.

source_issues.title: Next.js 16 post-build validation drops intermediate path segments from multi-segment Root Directory
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on Vercel CLI 50.43.0, Next.js 16.2.3. Build completes successfully but deploy is blocked by post-build validation ENOENT. Verified files exist at correct path on disk. Workaround requires symlinking in build script. Not reproduced on Next.js 14 — regression introduced in Next.js 16.

signals.topic: Production logs polluted by Node.js DEP0169 url.parse() deprecation warning on every function cold start
signals.summary: The Vercel Node.js serverless runtime logs a `DEP0169` deprecation warning (`url.parse()` is deprecated, prone to security implications) on cold start of every function at `level:error`. This creates noise in log searches and paging systems that filter by error level. Cannot be silenced from user code — only mitigation is global `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-deprecation` which suppresses all deprecation warnings.
aliases: Node.js runtime url.parse deprecation warning pollutes production logs
DEP0169 warning on every cold start creates error-level log noise
signals.review_reason: Production log pollution — every function cold start generates a level:error deprecation entry, degrading observability. Not a direct crash/breakage but causes real operational friction (alerting noise, log search pollution). Count=1, not a primary workflow blocker — correctly P2.

source_issues.title: Production Node.js runtime emits DEP0169 url.parse() deprecation warning on every cold start
source_issues.evidence: Every cold start logs a level:error entry across all Node.js 20+ functions. Cannot be silenced from user code; only global NODE_OPTIONS workaround exists. Affects log monitoring and alerting systems that filter by error level.

signals.topic: UI freezes on Hyprland/Wayland when in fullscreen and typing or opening popups
signals.summary: On Hyprland Wayland compositor, Zed UI freezes (5-10 seconds) when typing or triggering popups in fullscreen mode, only recovering after workspace switch. Not reproducible on X11. Blocks fullscreen workflow on the second-most popular Linux Wayland compositor.
signals.review_reason: Reproducible UI freeze blocking fullscreen workflow on Hyprland/Wayland, which is a major Linux desktop environment. The freeze is consistent (every time in fullscreen) and forces user to switch workspace as workaround, directly breaking the fullscreen editing experience.

source_issues.title: UI freezes on hyprland, when in fullscreen and typing/opening popups
source_issues.evidence: User reports UI freezes on Hyprland Wayland when typing or opening any popup in fullscreen mode. Freeze lasts 5-10 seconds or requires workspace switch to recover. Issue is reproducible 100% on Wayland fullscreen but does not occur on X11. Hyprland is the second-most popular Wayland compositor.

signals.topic: Agent tool path mismatch: system prompt advertises absolute paths but Agent tools require worktree-basename-relative paths, breaking all shell and search tool calls
signals.summary: When using Zed Agent on remote SSH connections, the system prompt tells the model to use absolute paths for tool calls, but all path-based tools (list_directory, shell, search) reject absolute paths and only accept worktree basename-relative paths. Every tool call fails silently, requiring manual intervention.
aliases: Zed Agent tool path bug remote SSH
list_directory path not in project absolute path
signals.review_reason: This bug completely breaks the Agent's path-based tool ecosystem (shell, search, list_directory) on remote SSH connections. Every tool call fails until the model guesses the correct basename-relative format. This is a critical workflow blocker for any user working with remote SSH projects via the Agent feature.

source_issues.title: Agent system prompt advertises absolute worktree paths but tools require basename-relative paths
source_issues.evidence: System prompt advertises absolute paths like /home/user/code/myproject but tools only accept 'myproject' (basename). All path tool calls fail: 'Path home/user/code/myproject is not in the project'. Frontier models recover after 2-3 retries; smaller models loop indefinitely. Core Agent functionality is broken.

signals.topic: Zed crashes on macOS Catalina at startup due to Metal shader nested struct compilation error, rendering the editor completely unusable on that OS version
signals.summary: Metal shader compiler on macOS 10.15 (Catalina) and earlier rejects vertex/fragment shaders with nested structs, causing a fatal compilation error at startup. No UI renders at all.
aliases: macOS Catalina startup crash Metal shader
signals.review_reason: Complete startup crash on macOS Catalina means the editor cannot even render its UI. This is a P0 severity for all users on that OS version. The issue has a full technical diagnosis and proposed fix.

source_issues.title: Flatten Metal shader vertex/fragment I/O structs for macOS Catalina compatibility
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states users on macOS Catalina see a 'fatal Metal compilation error at startup, preventing the editor from rendering anything.' The issue references #1 as the original bug. The fix requires flattening Metal struct definitions. This is a complete startup blocker for all users on macOS 10.15 and earlier.

signals.topic: MCP server running in Docker fails silently to reconnect after Docker restarts; toggle in AI settings does nothing with no error feedback
signals.summary: When a Docker-based MCP server (e.g., Laravel Sail) goes offline and comes back, Zed shows a red dot but the toggle switch fails to reconnect the process with zero user feedback. The user must delete and re-add the MCP configuration as a workaround.
aliases: MCP toggle does nothing after Docker restart
signals.review_reason: MCP reconnection failure with zero user feedback forces users to completely reconfigure MCP entries after any Docker restart. This breaks a core AI feature integration pattern (Docker-based dev tools like Laravel Sail, databases, etc.) and provides no diagnostic information to the user when reconnection fails.

source_issues.title: MCP running in Docker does not connect after Zed restart
source_issues.evidence: MCP shows red dot in AI settings after Docker restart; clicking the toggle does nothing (stays off, no animation, no error). No error message is shown anywhere. User must delete and re-add the MCP entry to reconnect. This is a common workflow for Docker-based development environments.

signals.topic: Fedora Linux (RPM) crashes on startup with Wasmtime panic 'unexpected kind: 129' after auto-installing HTML extension
signals.summary: On Fedora 44 with RPM package, Zed auto-installs the HTML extension on first run and immediately crashes in a worker thread with a Wasmtime panic. Reproducible with clean XDG profile and minimal settings.
aliases: Fedora RPM startup crash html extension
signals.review_reason: Complete startup crash on Fedora 44 (RPM install), one of the major Linux distributions. The crash is triggered by the auto-install of a built-in extension (HTML), making it unavoidable for any new Fedora RPM user. This is a critical onboarding blocker.

source_issues.title: Linux/Fedora: clean profile crashes after auto-installing HTML extension — Wasmtime panic 'unexpected kind: 129'
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible crash sequence: install Fedora RPM, start Zed, first-run setup triggers auto-install of HTML extension, crash in worker thread with Wasmtime panic. Confirmed reproducible with clean XDG profile and minimal settings across multiple project folders.
